notes: Mint tea pour reads as beer. The amber liquid sits in a tall pint glass with a foamy head, which on a brief that says 'no alcohol on screen' is a disqualifying misread. Re-render as pale green-gold tea in small decorated tea glasses, with fresh mint sprigs visible, a thin stream poured from height and no foam. Make it the hero slow-mo moment the brief asks for.
The first pour frame has an exploding splash that breaks the glass silhouette and looks chaotic rather than graceful. Replace it with a controlled, slow-motion arc.
Open flames burn in the foreground around the family dining table. They read as hazardous and nonsensical. Keep the fire in the oven and grill, and let the table glow from their warm light instead.

The windows show an old-world skyline of minarets and domes. The brand is a Toronto restaurant, so it reads as generic Orientalist pastiche. Use a warm Toronto street or neutral evening exterior, or frost the glass.

The end card text jumps from right-of-centre to left-of-centre between frames, and the left version sits over faces. Lock one position, give it a darkened or blurred plate behind it, and hold it steady for the full 3s.
'Concept by Unmissed, AI-assisted' appears twice on the end card, once in the corner and once under the tagline. Keep the corner label only.
The grill flare blows out to pure white and loses the skewers. Pull the highlights back so the meat and charcoal stay readable inside the burst, and make it clear the meat is lamb or chicken.

The steam-cloud shot over the stew is ambiguous: it is unclear what the cloud is coming from. Either clarify it as a tagine lid lift or cut it for a cleaner puffing-bread close-up in the clay oven, which the brief calls out and which is currently only shown already baked.
Keep the character designs consistent across shots: the young woman in the red hijab, the grandparents and the kids. Faces drift slightly between the kitchen and table shots.
Pacing reads mostly warm and mid-tempo. To land the 'voltage' direction, open harder with faster flare, spice and bread cuts, then contrast them with the slow pour.
